method: Read actual full source and original/diff; compared each changed paragraph in surrounding context. Candidate map not used as proof.

changed_blocks.before: **Reflect newly unlocked potential.** When summarising recently completed work, explicitly call out what each shipped issue **unblocked** — issues whose blockers cleared in the last 24-48 hours and are now ready (or one step closer to ready). This belongs in "Recently Completed" alongside the ship list, and these unlocked issues are flagged as *just-realised* potential (annotated "just unlocked by …") so the human/automation notices them — where they land in "Coming Up" / "Today's Focus" / "Ready to pick up" is the methodology's `pick-ordering` call, not wtf's.
changed_blocks.after: **Reflect newly unlocked potential.** In "Recently Completed", show what each shipped issue unblocked: blockers cleared within 24-48 hours, leaving dependents ready or closer to ready. Annotate these issues "just unlocked by …" as *just-realised* potential. Their placement in "Coming Up" / "Today's Focus" / "Ready to pick up" follows methodology `pick-ordering`, never wtf's judgement.

changed_blocks.before: Every invocation re-fetches the whole picture live per the shared **Always pull fresh** rule (gateway): every milestone, every In Progress / Blocked / Recently Completed / Coming Up issue, every blocker link, status field, and recent-activity timestamp. A briefing built on a partial or cached fetch is silently wrong, and the human acts on it.
changed_blocks.after: Re-fetch the whole picture live on every invocation (gateway → **Always pull fresh**): every milestone, In Progress / Blocked / Recently Completed / Coming Up issue, blocker link, status field and recent-activity timestamp. Never use a partial or cached fetch.

changed_blocks.before: **Two lanes, daily-driver first.** Sections 1–7 are the **L1 answer**: what shipped, what's stuck, your parked loose ends, and the 2–3 things to do today, plus a backlog-health read (methodology, structural diagnostics, calibration) drawn from tidy's cache. One section, the **automation preview** (§5b), answers a *different* question: is it worth handing the queue to `/faff-beep-boop`? It renders after the focus answer and never displaces it.
changed_blocks.after: **Two lanes, daily-driver first.** Sections 1–7 give the **L1 answer**: shipped/stuck work, parked loose ends, 2–3 priorities for today and backlog health (methodology, structural diagnostics, calibration) from tidy's cache. The **automation preview** (5b) follows without displacing that answer: is the queue worth handing to `/faff-beep-boop`?

changed_blocks.before:
Surface every issue faff has parked — whether by an overnight `/faff-beep-boop` run **or** interactively (a manual `/faff-prep` / `/faff-graft` that hit low confidence, an unresolved punt the user chose to leave, or a build-time ambiguity). The manual user parks too (L1 prep, L2 build), and that work must resurface here — not only beep-boop's.

**The `faff-parked` label is the spine of this section, not the run logs.** Every park — autonomous or interactive — applies the `faff-parked` label per the shared **Park / Unpark protocol** (gateway), so the tracker query catches them all regardless of how they were parked:
changed_blocks.after:
Surface every park, autonomous or interactive: overnight `/faff-beep-boop`, manual `/faff-prep` / `/faff-graft` low confidence, an unresolved punt the user left, or build-time ambiguity. Include human parks at L1 prep and L2 build.

**The `faff-parked` label is authoritative, not run logs.** Every autonomous or interactive park applies it (gateway → **Park / Unpark protocol**); query it to catch both:

changed_blocks.before: Surface every issue tagged `faff-awaiting-review` via a **live tracker label query** (this label is not `faff-parked`'s query above and is easy to miss otherwise — wtf's parked query is scoped to `faff-parked` only). **Distinct from Parked work above:** this is not a human park — it means the built work is durable (branch pushed) and the review is waiting on a **machine** (the provider) to recover, auto-resuming on the next `/faff-beep-boop` drain with no rebuild. For each: issue id + title, the outage-retry attempt count (`n`/`graft.review_outage_retry_limit`), and a note that no action is needed — it self-resolves next drain, or escalates to an ordinary park after the retry bound. Skip the section if none.
changed_blocks.after: Query `faff-awaiting-review` **live**, separately from `faff-parked`. These are provider outages: the built branch is pushed, review awaits the machine and resumes next `/faff-beep-boop` drain without rebuilding. For each issue, show id + title, retry attempt `n`/`graft.review_outage_retry_limit`, and that no action is needed: it self-resolves next drain or becomes an ordinary park after the retry bound. Skip if none.

changed_blocks.before: The prep-altitude twin of §4c above. Surface every issue tagged `faff-awaiting-spec-review` via a **live tracker label query** (a distinct label + query from `faff-awaiting-review`'s §4c — the two altitudes stay separable). **Distinct from Parked and §4c above:** not a human park, and not a stalled *build* — the spec is attached and durable on the tracker, review has not concluded, and the outage is waiting on a **machine** (the spec-review provider) to recover, auto-resuming on the next `/faff-beep-boop` drain with no re-spec. For each: issue id + title, the held-drain attempt count (`n`/`prep.spec_review_outage_hold_limit`), and a note that no action is needed — it self-resolves next prep drain, or escalates to an ordinary park past the hold limit. Skip the section if none.
changed_blocks.after: Query `faff-awaiting-spec-review` **live**, separately from `faff-awaiting-review` in 4c and from Parked work. The spec is attached durably to the tracker; review is unfinished while the provider recovers. Resume next `/faff-beep-boop` prep drain without re-speccing. Show each issue's id + title, held-drain attempt `n`/`prep.spec_review_outage_hold_limit`, and that no action is needed: it self-resolves next prep drain or becomes an ordinary park past the hold limit. Skip if none.

changed_blocks.before: Surface every **propose-only** ADR-admission candidate recorded by an autonomous `faff-graft` Step 3b run — a **loop-authored** ADR proposing to supersede a **human/legacy-provenance** ADR, which the admit gate correctly refused to auto-write (guardrails ratify only by human gesture; the loop never self-ratifies). Read `.faff/adr-proposals/*.json` (one file per candidate, keyed by the new ADR's number; written by graft, never by `/faff-wtf`). **Distinct from Parked / Awaiting-review above:** this isn't a stalled issue — the build that authored the proposing ADR already shipped; the proposal is a standing, git-native artifact (an ADR pair, not a tracker issue) waiting on a **ratification gesture**, not a build retry.
changed_blocks.after: Read `.faff/adr-proposals/*.json` for every **propose-only** autonomous graft Step 3b ADR-admission candidate: a loop-authored ADR proposing to supersede a human/legacy ADR, refused automatic writing because ratification requires a human gesture. Graft writes these files, one per new ADR number; wtf never does. The originating build already shipped. This standing git-native ADR pair awaits ratification, not a tracker issue or build retry.

changed_blocks.before: `disposition: reject` entries are informational only (already refused by the admit gate: challenge, by-level or ratchet; nothing to ratify) — mention a one-line count ("N supersession(s) refused by the admit gate — see the log") rather than itemising, unless appetite is `high`/`full` (prominent) per the gateway's appetite-graded-surfacing rule. Skip the section entirely if `.faff/adr-proposals/` is absent or empty.
changed_blocks.after: For `disposition: reject` (already refused by challenge, by-level or ratchet), nothing needs ratifying. Report a count: "N supersession(s) refused by the admit gate — see the log". Itemise prominently only at appetite `high`/`full` (gateway appetite-graded-surfacing rule). Skip the section if `.faff/adr-proposals/` is absent or empty.

changed_blocks.before:
Read the most recent tidy log (`.faff/logs/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMMSS-tidy.md`) for `backlog-diagnostics` findings. If no tidy ran this pass, request the `backlog-diagnostics` output from the configured methodology skill (default `faffter-noon-methodology-thematic`) — when it fires it joins the pass's batched methodology dispatch (**Methodology transport** above). Render a one-line status if all clean (`Structural diagnostics: clean ✓`); otherwise render the findings in the format that output defines.

Repeat-parks, orphaned+repeat-parked, and **chain-gap** findings (any sub-type — sub-ticket / upstream / downstream / peer) additionally surface in `### Heads up` so the user sees the urgent patterns prominently, not just in the diagnostics dump. Chain gaps are first-class Heads-up material: when a ticket's spec references work no ticket tracks, picking up the ticket leaves the broader purpose unfulfilled with no breadcrumb for what's next. Tag each Heads-up chain-gap entry with the sub-type so the human can scan-read.
changed_blocks.after:
Read the latest tidy log (`.faff/logs/YYYY-MM-DD/HHMMSS-tidy.md`) for `backlog-diagnostics`. If no tidy ran this pass, request that output from the configured methodology (default `faffter-noon-methodology-thematic`) within the pass's batched dispatch (**Methodology transport**). Render `Structural diagnostics: clean ✓` if clean; otherwise use the output's findings format.

Also surface repeat-parks, orphaned+repeat-parked and every **chain-gap** sub-type (sub-ticket / upstream / downstream / peer) in `### Heads up`, beyond the diagnostics section. Tag each chain-gap entry with its sub-type so missing work is visible before the human picks a focus issue.
